newsitem.title: USA: Westinghouse loss narrows in quarter.
newsitem.headline: Westinghouse loss narrows in quarter.

text.p: Westinghouse Electric Corp. said Friday its losses narrowed slightly in the first quarter as the company's robust CBS Radio group helped offset weakness at its television stations, industries and technology and power systems businesses.
The net loss narrowed to $151 million, or 23 cents a share, in the quarter ended March 31 from $181 million, or 41 cents a share, in the year-ago period.
The Pittsburgh-based company had a loss from continuing operations of $151 million, compared with a year-ago loss of $114 million, or 26 cents per share, excluding special items.
Including the year-end 1996 acquisition of Infinity Broadcasting, sales rose 18 percent to $2.2 billion.
Westinghouse's media group earned $110 million before interest, taxes and other items, unchanged from the 1996 period.
Infinity's contribution to earnings was offset by weakness at the company's television network, caused by poor ratings and an unfavourable accounting method for programme rights.

Excluding Infinity, sales in the media group rose 5 percent for the quarter. Sales for the CBS radio group surged 18 percent, far outperforming the radio industry. Pretax earnings soared 38 percent to $91 million.
"CBS Radio exceeded our most optimistic expectations, and is setting the pace of growth for the entire industry," said Michael Jordan, chairman and chief executive officer.

"At the CBS TV network, demographic ratings are beginning to improve, positioning us well for the 1997-1998 advertising market. At our television stations, it is apparent that the extensive actions underway are beginning to have a positive effect, with 10 of our 14 stations showing higher (pretax earnings) performance."
At the TV network, earnings fell due to lower audience levels in key demographic categories and cost increases mainly associated with sports and special events, it said.

Television revenues slid 4 percent on a same-station basis. Last year's first quarter gained from political advertising. Despite lower revenues, earnings were flat due to cost cuts and other improvements at the TV stations.

Earnings fell at Westinghouse's other media businesses, which include Eyemark and CBS Cable -- formerly Group W Satellite Communications. This includes a loss of $10 million from the expansion of the CBS TeleNoticias cable network and the development and launch of Eye On People, a new cable channel that debuted on March 31.
The Industries and Technology Group lost $59 million, compared with a $1 million loss in the year-ago quarter, excluding special charges in 1996.
About $50 million of the current loss was due to a reevaluation of a complex international energy systems project, the company said.

Operating losses at Power Systems, which includes the Power Generation and Energy Systems businesses, grew due to delays in international project closings. Year-ago earnings were also boosted by a large nuclear fuel reload order.

Westinghouse said profits at its Thermo King division were enhanced by last year's two European acquisitions as well as lower material costs and greater productivity. Orders also rose 5 percent due to a large container order and strong service parts business, it said.
Westinghouse's stock slipped by 12.5 cents to $17.75 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
